A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and DoRI naming. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–K are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on adversarial embeddings, memorization mitigation, model locality, and image quality, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds Stable Diffusion 2.0, regional template-memorization, and broader generation-quality evaluations.

M1.justification: The core adversarial-embedding and mitigation algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix I.9 introduces Ours+FT, which adds an ordinary fine-tuning stage on non-memorized images after mitigation to recover generation quality.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained LAION-derived memorization and COCO evaluations, v3 adds HPDv3 prompt categories and T2I-CompBench++ tasks. These extend coverage to preference-oriented generation and explicit compositional requirements, including attribute binding, spatial relationships, and numeracy.

E2.justification: The established NeMo, Wanda, ESD, Concept Ablation, SISS, and UnlearnDiffAtk/GCG comparisons remain. Tables 19–21 additionally evaluate Ours+FT alongside Ours and the retained comparators; this is an added comparison variant, not a new external mitigation baseline.

E3.justification: V3 adds SD2.0 evaluations using 32 SSCD-filtered image–text pairs and stronger NeMo settings, foreground/background SSCD and memorization-rate evaluation for template memorization, and new preference-ranking and compositional-alignment protocols. Appendix I.9 specifies 1,000 images per HPDv3 category and ten images per compositional prompt. The original 50-step DoRI setting remains.

E4.justification: New analyses examine regional template replication, extend paraphrase-quality assessment to the proposed mitigation, and test whether supplementary fine-tuning repairs utility without restoring memorization (H.2, I.8–I.9). Qualitative optimization-progress examples are also added. The extensive pruning, loss-component, LoRA, and UnlearnDiffAtk analyses already existed in v2.

E5.justification: V3 omits v2's explicit median-of-max aggregation statement and statement that adversarial-optimization seeds are varied. Ten seeded generations for memorization rate, five-seed Wanda sampling, and existing uncertainty entries remain. No increase in repeated runs or new inferential statistics is documented.

E6.justification: The matched SD1.4 tables largely retain their numerical results. New SD2.0 results report adversarial memorization rates of 1.00 for NeMo, 0.53 for Wanda, and 0.06 for the proposed mitigation (Table 14). Regional template results and Tables 18–21 add substantial findings on replication, quality degradation, and recovery through Ours+FT; these are additional evaluations, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: The diffusion losses, SISS formulation, runtime expression, and formal locality metrics retain their mathematics. Renaming the diffusion loss does not change its definition. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation accompanies the added empirical metrics.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain. V3 drops the introduction's explicit first-method assertion and omits the conclusion's caution that every possible form of locality cannot be ruled out. Its main locality conclusion is consequently less qualified, although Appendix A retains the layer-scope limitation.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning deletion requirements, membership inference, and the distinction between fixed-weight probing and relearning attacks (Appendix A). Section 4.1 and G.3 introduce explanations involving spiky representations and surrogate-induced generalization. Appendix I.9 newly acknowledges generation-quality degradation and discusses its recovery, materially expanding the utility trade-off analysis.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit project-code URL, SD2.0 filtering/pruning details, and Ours+FT settings: 80,000 images, one epoch, learning rate 10^-6, and batch size 128. However, v2's explicit 30,000-prompt COCO quality-evaluation description disappears. Hardware, software, Dockerfile disclosure, and core pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds targeted connections to relearning attacks and representation-based explanations, plus references supporting regional memorization and the new quality benchmarks. Some references supporting the removed metric-description passage disappear. The principal positioning against pruning and concept unlearning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V3 retitles the paper, changes Dori to DoRI, edits the introduction and conclusion, adds appendix navigation and takeaway summaries, and promotes the earlier Appendix J.4 discussion into Section 4.4.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reformats the main paper into two columns, simplifies main tables, and redesigns plot legends and placement. Earlier appendix plots are split, merged, or promoted; the weight-count plots become a combined percentage display. New evaluation tables and qualitative panels are added, and several Wanda example panels are replaced.

improvement.justification: The second-model tests, regional template evaluation, and broader quality benchmarks strengthen validation and reveal utility costs that v2's FID-focused discussion missed. These benefits outweigh limited reporting regressions, but inconsistencies constrain the gain: Appendix A still claims a single-model study, some protocol details disappear, and Table 21 claims superiority over Wanda despite Ours scoring lower on seven of eight compositional measures.
